subject: Re: Follow-up: Cost/TCO vs Hyperscaler for FinPay POC
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Cost/TCO vs Hyperscaler for FinPay POC

Samir —

Thanks for the time today — good call. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we have alignment before the POC: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: validate latency and unit cost for FinPay’s transaction enrichment pipeline (avg prompt ~1.2k tokens, expected peak ~100 req/s).
- Key eval criteria: per-1M token cost, p50/p95 latency, and ability to reduce unit cost via batching + prefix caching.
- Competitive concern: FinPay is evaluating Hyperscaler A + self-hosted inference alongside Redwood.

High-level Redwood differentiators we discussed
- Unit economics: Hosted Redwood estimate (production config): ~$450 per 1M tokens (including average batching and cache savings). Hyperscaler A estimate for comparable model/config: ~$1,200 per 1M tokens (hosted endpoint list price).
- Batching & throughput: Continuous batching on our runtime commonly reduces per-token CPU/GPU overhead by ~30-45% depending on request concurrency; at 100 req/s we expect the lower end of that range unless you enable burst batching which improves it further.
- Prefix/KV caching: For FinPay’s repetitive enrichment prompts we typically see 15-35% effective cache hit rate in POCs if the prompt templates and user IDs overlap; this translates almost directly to per-token cost reduction on repeated prefixes.
- Deployment flexibility: Hosted for fast time-to-value; Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable throughput and lower unit cost for sustained traffic.

Requested next tests (proposed POC scope)
1) Unit-cost TCO run: synthetic 1M token run using your average prompt length (1.2k tokens) to get per-1M token charge and aggregation across p50/p95 latencies.
2) Batching sensitivity: run with batching disabled vs default continuous batching to measure per-token delta.
3) Cache effectiveness: run a 100k-request workload with ~30% repeated prefixes to estimate cache hit rate and effective cost reduction.
4) Dedicated baseline: estimate Dedicated pricing for a 6- and 12-month committed scenario and compare blended TCO.

Attachments I’m sending: a TCO model (TCO_model_v3.xlsx) and a short competitive one-pager (Redwood-competitive-one-pager.pdf). I’ll follow up with Marcus to include pricing details for Dedicated/reserved capacity.

Proposed next meeting: Thu Jul 2 or Fri Jul 3 — 30 minutes to review the TCO outputs together and finalize the POC plan. What works for you?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap and the model. A few clarifying questions from our side before we run the POC: 
- Can you break down the $450/1M tokens into hosted (on-demand) vs dedicated amortized costs? We want to show procurement two options.
- For the batching delta you mentioned (30-45%), is that on average or do you have example runs at ~100 req/s we can point to?
- On caching: curious what assumptions you used to estimate 15-35% — how is that measured in short POCs?

Also, we’d like the TCO sheet to include our expected concurrency profile (peak 100 req/s, avg 35 req/s) and two retention scenarios (1 month KV cache vs 24 hours).

We’re available Fri Jul 3 10-11am PT for the 30-minute review. Send a calendar invite and any additional pricing sheets.

samir@finpay.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Cost/TCO vs Hyperscaler for FinPay POC

Samir —

Great — Fri Jul 3 10:00am PT works. Calendar invite sent. Quick answers + what we changed in the attached TCO model: 

1) Cost breakdown (high-level) - values are estimates for planning, final numbers will depend on POC telemetry:
- Hosted (Redwood, default): ~$450 per 1M tokens (this assumes typical batching + a 20% effective cache hit from repeated prefixes for FinPay-like templates).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): blended per-1M token equivalent of ~$320 per 1M tokens with a 12-month commit at the expected utilization (includes infra amortization + reserved discount).
- Hyperscaler A: ~$1,200 per 1M tokens (public endpoint list pricing for comparable large model family; does not assume aggressive batching).

2) Batching examples: We ran an internal benchmark at ~100 req/s with 1.5k average tokens and saw a ~37% reduction in per-token GPU time using our continuous batching + kernel scheduling compared to single-request throughput. I’ve noted that benchmark source in the TCO model comments.

3) Cache assumptions: For short POCs we instrument prefix overlap by replaying a representative sample of recent requests (or synthetic data with repeated templates). A 15% conservative hit assumes light template reuse; 30% uses product-typical overlap we see in finance enrichment where customer IDs and templates repeat. The TCO_model_v3.xlsx has toggles for 10/20/30% hit scenarios.

Next tests we’ll run for the POC (to be executed by Redwood with FinPay-provided request samples):
- 1M token throughput run with average prompt 1.2k tokens (baseline hosted).
- Batching off vs batching on run to capture delta (same input sequence).
- Cache stress run with 30% repeated prefixes to calculate effective hit rate and cost delta.
- Dedicated estimate run (pricing sheet attached) for 6mo and 12mo commit scenarios.

Attachments included in this email: TCO_model_v3.xlsx, redwood-pricing-2026.xlsx.

See you Fri at 10 - invite contains the dial-in.

Cheers,
Aditya

Samir / Aditya —

Couple quick technical + pricing notes to flag ahead of the call: 
- Quantization & inference stack: For most of the open model families we support 4-bit quantization (with Redwood runtime optimizations). In internal perf runs for similar models, 4-bit gives ~1.1x-1.2x throughput improvement vs 8-bit quant, with negligible quality delta for retrieval/structured-enrichment tasks. We’ll include quantization settings in the POC config so you can toggle them.
- Dedicated pricing note: I added redwood-pricing-2026.xlsx with a worked example for a 6-month and 12-month commit. For a 12-month committed Reserved pool we can push the blended per-1M token effective price to roughly $260-300 depending on utilization and instance mix; I’ve included a conservative sensitivity table in the sheet.
- Next tests: we should also capture latency percentiles (p50/p95), not just average. For FinPay use-case, 99th percentile is less relevant than p95 for SLAs but we’ll capture it.

I’m available on the call to walk through the Dedicated numbers.

Marcus
